title: Pin-loaded lug, D/W = 0.5 (3D solid)
description:
Pin-loaded lug (clevis eye) in bearing. 3D solid.
Geometry file (STEP): the full 3D lug, thickness b = 10 mm along z (z from 0 to 10 mm).
Purpose: a steel lug (the eye of a clevis joint) of thickness b = 10 mm. A straight shank of width W = 40 mm (x from -20 mm to 20 mm) rises from its base at y = 0 and ends in a semicircular head of outer radius 20 mm centred at (x, y) = (0, 60 mm). A pin hole of diameter D = 20 mm is concentric with the head. The bore is split into its upper half (y >= 60 mm, the side away from the base) and its lower half.
Material: steel, linear elastic and isotropic, E = 200 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.3.
Supports: the base (y = 0) is fixed, all displacement components zero (the lug is machined from a much stiffer block).
Load: the pin pulls the lug in +y with a total force P = 20 kN. Model the pin bearing as a radial pressure on the upper half of the bore only, cosine distributed: p = p0 cos(theta), where theta is the angle from the +y direction measured at the hole centre (so cos(theta) = (y - 60 mm) / a with a = 10 mm the hole radius), and p0 = 2P / (pi a b) so that the resultant of the pressure is exactly P. The pressure pushes the material away from the hole centre; the lower half of the bore is free.
Analysis: linear static, small displacements, no contact (the pin is not modelled).
The pressure is uniform through the thickness. Exploiting symmetry is allowed.
Report:
  peak_hoop_stress: the maximum value of the maximum principal stress s1 on the bore surface (both halves) [Pa];
  lug_elongation: the average y-displacement of the loaded upper half of the bore [m].
